correctness.rationale: For kU>μ the bracket is positive at 0 and negative at 1 and has a unique simple positive root. For τ>0 this follows from the negative leading quadratic coefficient; at τ=0 the bracket is instead affine with negative slope −k(U+V), a minor missing qualification in the proof on line 72, not an exception to the result. Evaluating the bracket at U/(U+V) confirms the opposite signs of the degree response and g, with exact degree invariance at a zero. Under the odds substitution the coefficients of q^0,q^3,q^4,q^5 are strictly negative and only q,q² can switch signs. Descartes therefore counts at most two positive zeros including multiplicities. A/B goes to infinity on the boundary of its positive-B domain, including at infinity if present; an attained minimum thus creates a double root, both unique and nondegenerate by the count. Above threshold it creates positive sign between two simple roots and only there. Expanding the double root and multiplying the width by the odds-to-distrust Jacobian gives (4). Independent spot check: differentiate f(η)=η(1−η)^3(1+2η) at 1/√10 and evaluate 1/f and sqrt(−8/(s_c² f'')); these give 6.05932512326131218 and 0.271452770413063155. Exact signs of 8f−1 at 159/1000,160/1000,1/10,3/10,1/2,7/10 were −,+,−,+,0,−. This check corroborates the example; it does not establish the quantified theorem.
residual_risks: Fixed triangle incidence and independent signs in a homogeneous deterministic closure; no conclusion for subcritical or bistable equilibria or finite stochastic networks.

value.rationale: Resolves the practical ambiguity left by an isolated crossing: across all admissible rates, no two disconnected distrust regimes can exhibit suppression at fixed triangle exposure; the result says exactly when suppression first becomes possible and its onset scale.
